page: Microsoft Azure D16lds_v7 is a compute-focused virtual machine belonging to the Dldsv7 server family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor built on the x86_64 architecture, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. It is equipped with a massive 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE and AMX_INT8) for accelerated matrix operations, and hardware-accelerated cryptography via AES and SHA_NI.

This server is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. For local storage, the instance includes a bundled 945 GB NVMe SSD, providing fast local read and write capabilities. The hardware profile is designed for workloads requiring high CPU clock speeds and local disk access but with lower memory capacity requirements.

Benchmark results show strong single-threaded performance, with gzip compression reaching 32.42 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 13.98 GB/sec. Multi-core stress-ng CPU performance registers at 15943.77, while memory read-only bandwidth for cached small blocks reaches 1177.65 GB/sec. The instance demonstrates average performance in database operations (8069.91 on Passmark) and Redis SET operations (27.33 million operations per second). It is well-suited for compute-bound tasks, web serving, software compilation, and lightweight database workloads that benefit from fast local NVMe storage but do not require large memory footprints.
